changes.comment: BREAKING: code organization refactor stage 8c, item 1: `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` is deleted, and so is `dreamux onboard`'s `--config-dir` option; `dreamux uninstall --config-dir` is deleted too, by inference — it has nothing left to relocate once `config.json` is root-derived. `config.json` now always lives at `<DREAMUX_ROOT>/config.json` (default `~/.dreamux/config.json`, unchanged only for an install that set neither `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` nor `DREAMUX_ROOT`); the managed-service unit now writes `DREAMUX_ROOT` instead of `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR`, taking the value from the environment of the process that runs `dreamux daemon install` or `dreamux onboard` (`~/.dreamux` when unset); `dreamux uninstall` now also removes the whole root directory itself, not just its contents. Before this change `DREAMUX_ROOT` relocated only state, run, cache and logs, `config.json` came from `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.dreamux`, and the managed-service unit that `dreamux daemon install` wrote carried no `DREAMUX_ROOT`, so a managed service ran with `.dreamux` under its `HOME` as its root unless its environment supplied a `DREAMUX_ROOT` by another route (a unit drop-in, an environment file, or the service manager's own environment). Scenario 1: an install that set `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` to a path other than the root it ran with — after upgrade `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` is silently ignored, so the daemon looks for `config.json` under the root instead of the operator's configured directory. If no `config.json` exists there, the daemon fails on an ordinary missing-file error that never mentions `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` or what moved, and the unit's `Restart=on-failure` loops; if a `config.json` already exists there (for example from an earlier default-path `dreamux onboard`), the daemon starts silently against that unrelated file instead. Scenario 2: an operator who exports `DREAMUX_ROOT` in their shell (profile, direnv, a foreground `dreamux serve`) while `config.json` stayed in `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.dreamux` — `dreamux serve` and `dreamux daemon install` run from that shell now look for `config.json` under the exported root and fail on the same missing-file error (`dreamux doctor` reports it); and if the operator moves `config.json` there and re-runs `dreamux daemon install`, the shell's root is written into the unit, so the service moves to a root it never used: its durable state (dispatcher identities, Teams, Workflow runs, `access.json`) stays behind in the old root and the service comes up on a root that holds none of it. Rebuild: keep the root the old service actually used — do not assume it is the `DREAMUX_ROOT` your shell exports. (1) Find that root from the environment the old daemon actually ran with. For a managed service, read it from the running process (on Linux `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$(systemctl --user show -p MainPID --value dreamux)/environ | grep -E '^(DREAMUX_ROOT|HOME)='`) or, when it is not running, from everything that defines that environment: the installed unit and any drop-ins (`systemctl --user cat dreamux`), any `EnvironmentFile` they name, and the user manager's own environment (`systemctl --user show-environment`); on macOS, the plist `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.excited.dreamux.plist` and `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/dev.excited.dreamux`. A unit written by an earlier build has no `DREAMUX_ROOT` entry of its own, so unless one of those sources supplies it the root is `.dreamux` under the service's `HOME` (normally `~/.dreamux`). A foreground `dreamux serve` used the `DREAMUX_ROOT` of the shell that started it, else `~/.dreamux`. Confirm the root by checking that `<root>/state/` holds your dispatcher directories. (2) Put `config.json` at `<that root>/config.json`: move it from the old service's `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` path (found the same way) when that names another directory (keep mode 0600, create parent directories as needed); there is nothing to move when it already sits in that root. (3) Re-run `dreamux daemon install` (or `dreamux onboard` again) from a shell whose `DREAMUX_ROOT` is that same root — or unset, when the root is `~/.dreamux` — so the unit is rewritten with the right `DREAMUX_ROOT`, then run `dreamux daemon restart`. For a foreground `dreamux serve`, export the same root in the shell that starts it. Only a deliberate change of root moves durable state: with the service stopped, move the old root's `state/` to `<new root>/state/` (`run/` is volatile, `cache/` is rebuildable, and `logs/` is diagnostics, so none of them needs to move) and `config.json` to `<new root>/config.json`, then do step (3) with `DREAMUX_ROOT` set to the new root; without the `state/` move the service starts on empty state.
